source_text: Longitudines numeratae a Meridiano primo ... qui a Parisiensi removetur 20 ... versus Occidentem
source_text_locator: bottom border of view f2, transcribed from the native raster
conversion_basis: Ferro as used by 18th-century French and German cartographers = exactly 20 degrees west of the Paris meridian, per the sheet's own statement
conversion_source: Paris meridian longitude from the IERS/IGN value already used by mapgen (PRIME_MERIDIANS in historical_georeference.py, established in MAPGEN-012 and validated on the 1756 Vaugondy sheet at Dresden)
notes: Recorded as data so no bare constant decides where a historical map lands. Applies to the Vaugondy 1756 sheet as well, which states the same convention.

source_text: Ferro meridian, 20 degrees west of Paris
the plate carries no printed meridian statement; the graduations themselves are the only evidence
source_text_locator: top and bottom graduated bands, 9-21 and 10-20 degrees, and the side bands 35-44 degrees; three of the numerals were read at magnification and matched to the pixel (iberia_lerouge_plate_graticule_observations.csv)
conversion_basis: EMPIRICAL. Longitudes read off the engraved graduations were compared with the reference coordinates of the observed settlements; the median offset is the plate's own meridian.
conversion_source: MAPGEN-026, iberia_lerouge_prime_meridian_candidate_audit.csv, scored on FIT + MODEL_SELECTION with the blind set untouched
notes: Ferro at 20 degrees west of Paris scores about twice as badly as the empirical offset (median 52.8 km against 28.6 km), so Ferro is recorded as plausible but not adopted. NONE of this enters the transform: the georeference maps pixels straight to Greenwich degrees from observed features, exactly as MAPGEN-018R requires, and border ticks are never used as 2D control points.

source_text: neither sheet prints a meridian statement; the longitudes are read off the engraved graduation
source_text_locator: top and bottom graduated bands of both sheets, 7 deg 20 min to 11 deg 40 min
conversion_basis: EMPIRICAL. The offset is carried as one extra unknown in the longitude system beside the control points, and solved for; four estimators over two sheets
notes: Ferro at 20 degrees west of Paris predicts 17.662771 deg west; the four estimators average 17.681961, a difference of 1.66 km at 39 N. Diagnostic only - the transform maps pixels straight to Greenwich.
